evidence_items.publisher: National Venture Capital Association, using PitchBook data
evidence_items.locator: Key Findings, paragraph on venture-backed exits
evidence_items.explanation: The release documents constrained liquidity, reduced distributions, and weak fund formation, supporting the antecedent in its ordinary qualitative sense. It does not establish that these constraints make continued AI financing impossible.

evidence_items.publisher: National Venture Capital Association, using PitchBook data
evidence_items.explanation: The same release reports strong investment concentrated in AI, continuing fundraising, and exit value more than double the prior year. This limits the literal present-tense language and shows that liquidity pressure coexisted with substantial AI funding, although much investment involved nontraditional investors.

unresolved_gaps: No quantified link establishes that VC liquidity constraints create an unavoidable shortfall relative to continuing AI funding needs.
US findings do not establish the claim globally.
The evidence does not distinguish a temporary liquidity shortage from a lasting financing limit.
Investment into VC-backed companies is not entirely supplied by traditional VC funds.
